utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We are now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Your Honours, while the witness is coming into the courtroom, I would just take this opportunity to remind everyone that, as I indicated in my letter dated 28 November, this witness does have some health issues that may require us to take a more frequent break, if need be, due to his health conditions. I just put that out at this point in the event that it becomes apparent that we might need to break. I will ask to do so.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Good morning, sir. May the witness please make the declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good morning. I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You may be seated. Yes, Mr. Neuner.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Good morning, Mr. Alihodzic.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Good morning.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: For the record, sir, could you please state your full name and tell us your date and place of birth?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Ekrem Alihodzic, born on the 9th of April, 1951, in the village of Kljucani Vakuf, Municipality of Sanski Most, Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, before we begin, let me tell you that the Chamber is aware of your medical situation, and if at any point in time you need to take a break, simply tell us and we will accommodate that.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I understand. Thank you for your understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Also, sir, I think I speak on behalf of everyone when I say we will do our best to ensure that your testimony finishes as quickly as possible. In order to do that, I would ask you to please focus on the question asked and answer only that question, in order to expedite proceedings. I can assure you that you'll be given a full opportunity to explain anything and also that there very well might be follow-up questions. But if you could please focus your attention on the question asked and answer only that question, things will move a little bit more quickly. Mr. Alihodzic, did you join the JNA at any point in time, and if so, when did you join that armed force?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I just be of assistance, Your Honours. Could my colleague, Mr. Mundis, lead the witness through these questions so that we can deal with all of this faster? Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Mundis. Thank you for understanding.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Ms. Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, did you join the JNA in 1970?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I graduated from Secondary Military School in 1970.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, I see you taking out the list of dates from your wallet. Perhaps if you could just put that down for the moment and not refer to that. I'll simply ask you some questions. I believe if you need to look at the list of dates, the Chamber might allow you to do so, but I would simply ask if you -- that you not look at that for the moment, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: [In English] Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, after graduating from the Secondary Military School in 1970, did you remain a member of the JNA until 1991?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And from 1972 until the end of your period with the JNA in 1991, was your specialisation in military security and military police work within the JNA?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, on or about 5 January 1993, did you report to the 3rd Corps Command in Zenica?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: At that time, were you assigned to the 333rd Mountain Brigade in Kacuni as assistant to the commander?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but not as assistant commander, but let's put it this way, coordinator, a person who was supposed to help the commander of the then 333rd Mountain Brigade.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, on or about 4 May 1993, did you in fact become the commander of the 333rd Mountain Brigade of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And on 22 September 1993, you were wounded, which resulted in your being hospitalised until 10 January 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And following this hospitalisation, you returned to the 333rd Mountain Brigade and remained the commander of that unit until 5 October 1994; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alihodzic, from 5 October 1994 until 31 March 1995, you served as the chief of the Counter-Intelligence Department within the 3rd Corps Military Security Department; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: It was called "The Department for Counter-Intelligence Affairs," or, rather, "The Organ for Counter-intelligence Affairs."

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And that organ, the counter-intelligence organ, was part of the Security Department of the 3rd Corps; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: It was within the department of the service. I am using the exact denominations from the establishment of the Command of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alihodzic, is it correct that on 31 March 1995, you were appointed as the 3rd Corps assistant commander for military security?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Correct, chief of the Department of the Military Security and assistant commander for military security, which would be more in line with the rules and what the rules exactly say.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, you remained as the chief of the Department of Military Security and assistant commander for military security of the 3rd Corps from 31 March 1995 until 16 August 1995; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And from 16 August 1995 until 22 March 1996, you served as the commander of the 37th Division of the 3rd Corps, based in Tesanj?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The command of the division was in Tesanj, and units were deployed in a broader locality, and it is true that I had that duty.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, can you briefly tell us -- I want to focus your attention now on the period from 31 March 1995 until 16 August 1995, when you were the assistant commander for military security in the 3rd Corps. Can you tell us, sir, what your responsibilities entailed during this time period as the assistant commander for military security?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: My responsibilities were regulated through the Rules of Service, of the rules governing military security. In terms of segments, they were divided into three areas, if I can put it that way. The first is counter-intelligence protection and self-protection of commands and units. The second area dealt with staff security and military security affairs. And the third area was analytical and information activities. This was in line with the organisational and establishment structure of the department for security of the 3rd Corps. Later, this division was transformed into a department for military security. I would really need the Rules of Service for the organs of military security to speak thoroughly about all the authority that was vested in these organs. At this point in time, I cannot give you a more accurate answer without resorting to the rules themselves.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would ask that the witness now be shown the document 364 marked for identification. 364 marked for identification, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This is a primary document -- or, rather, secondary document that was created based on a primary document. This is a daily report drafted by the Military Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: When you say, sir, "the Military Security Service," the military security service of what organisation or entity?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The 3rd Corps, the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please go to the last page of this document in Bosnian and page 12 of the English version, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry, but in French I heard "a secondary document," and in the transcript, in English, I see "primary document." Could you specify, please, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, this document, would you characterise this as a primary document or a secondary document? And can you explain for us what exactly those terms mean.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This is a secondary document, and I'll explain what this is very gladly. In a series of documents, I believe, and the documents that will be presented to me later on, we will see that those documents have the same nature. Reports of the military security organs of the 3rd Corps who wrote to the 3rd Corps wrote their daily reports that treated security matters. This would be an initial document of a division, of a brigade, also one of the 16 brigades. The Corps at that time had 16 brigades, or two divisions, then independent battalions. There were 16 independent battalions, including four from those two divisions I mentioned. Then there was a number of platoons of military police, then two companies of the military police, one battalion of the military police, and they all submitted to the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps, their daily reports, in this form. Then, finally, after the department of the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps, all of this would be read out, then it would be sent to the analysis people or, rather, the organ of security of the 3rd Corps, and then a report would be compiled on the basis of all of this. Now, that can have -- that can lead to certain comments, this kind of comment and that kind of comment. This is a product of the person who wrote the report. It is possible that one organ considers this this way, and had it been written by someone else, it would have been different. But, at any rate, an effort was made to write it realistically; some things that were superfluous were omitted.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me, if I could, interrupt you there, sir, because I think you've explained that difference to us. If you could return to the document on the screen, and I would ask you, sir: Whose name appears at the bottom of this document we've been looking at, 364 MFI?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: In the left-hand corner are the initials of the person who did this, and the other initials were the initials of the person who typed this out.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, we have great trouble hearing the witness because other microphones are on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could scroll over to the left of the document, please, on the B/C/S. No, just to the left. And also on the English, if we could go to the full left side.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise the initials of the person who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I see an "R," the letter "R." The next letter is not discernible or legible. I can only assume -- now, is it a "C" with a diacritic? I don't know. I cannot see this letter properly, so I cannot fully identify it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could then go to the right-hand side of the document in Bosnian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, I'd ask you if you recognise -- if you recognise whose type-signed name appears on this document.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: My name and last name were typed out on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I take it, sir, that some of the characters would represent diacritics in the Bosnian language and that's why they don't appear to be legible on this copy or understandable on this copy.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right. That reflected the state of logistics and the possibilities of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could then go back, please, to the first page in both English and Bosnian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, Mr. Alihodzic, I'd like to focus your attention on the top half of this document, please. Can you tell us, if you know, what the stamp on the right-hand side, in the middle of the document, indicates?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The stamp on the upper right-hand side is recognisable to me. It denotes the Administration of the Service of Military Security of the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, and, at any rate, this is a stamp, and everything that is written here and these lines that you can see here, that was added in, so to speak, outside this secondary document that was created in the service of the military security of the 3rd Corps, after it was sent to the administration. I don't know where this stamp was affixed, who wrote all of this and so on.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter did not hear the end of the answer.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you repeat the end of the answer, sir? You said you didn't know where the stamp was affixed, who wrote all of this. Was there anything you wanted to add to that answer, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: There is nothing for me to add. This is the statement I have to make. This is my final answer: When I wrote the document and it was sent through my organs to the superior service of military security, everything that happened further on with the document, that is their own affair, and I cannot give my comments with regard to that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. The Prosecution would ask this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, it will become Exhibit number 364.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask now the witness be shown Exhibit 580, Exhibit 580, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, do you see this document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask if we could have the full-page version of the Bosnian be shown, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, whose signature appears on this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: My signature is on this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please scroll to the bottom paragraph on the first page of the English version, and if we could focus in on the bottom half of the document or the middle half of the -- the middle part of the document in Bosnian, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the reference in the middle of this document to captives who are under the control of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you comment upon that part of this document which you signed, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: My comment would be that there were captures and that the organ of security of the 35th Division was stopped or, rather, he had no access to prisoners of war, as far as I can remember at this point in time, after all this time.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, Mr. Alihodzic, when you say he had no access to prisoners of war, who are you referring to, and why was it that that person had no access to prisoners of war?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: We mean the security organ of the 35th Division. Now, why? Due to the behaviour of individuals and the fact that they did not allow this to happen, they -- from this detachment, I don't know these specific persons, so I cannot give a broader explanation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. If we could now scroll up to the top of the document in both English and B/C/S.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I would again, sir, ask you if you can tell us anything about the stamp that appears under the words "Strictly Confidential." What does that stamp indicate or tell us, if you know?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Again, how should I define this as briefly as possible? This is the stamp of the Military Security Administration. I recognise it because I read this here. That is what is written here. Whether that is really the stamp that was used by this service and what was done and what was not done, that is not what I can comment. This was not an integral part of my work and what I established and so on. Do you understand what I'm saying? But, please, when I write a document and when I send it to the administration, well, I would not go into comments of this kind, because I can now start a debate and -- in this sense, the General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina, with its administration in Sarajevo, had its head and this stamp, and this same administration had a forward command post in Kakanj, and this stamp could have been used in Kakanj as well. And it is for that reason that I am saying this, because this does not make it possible for me to be very precise in my answer, and then I don't want to sin against myself or anyone else in this court. So, please, if we can be careful about this kind of thing when we are discussing it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's a matter of interpretation, if I may. Page 29, line 8, the witness said: "That was not part of my work," whereas here it says: "This was part of my work." And then that would create confusion.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Fair enough. I appreciate that, Madam Vidovic. Thank you. If this document could now be put away, and I would ask that the witness be shown Exhibit 858, Exhibit 858.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, may I intervene? Could you show the lower initials on this document that we discussed? Ganibegovic, Ibro, was the person who processed this document from the security organ of the 3rd Corps, and it says here "cc'd number 1" circle around it, "Organ of Security, Bezbednost," I think this is an "S" with a diacritic, "Sh", something seems to be changing here. "Kakanj," it says "Kakanj." And you understand me, we have this same stamp in the heading. That is what makes it equivocal, whether this stamp was affixed in Sarajevo or in Kakanj, and that is very meaningful. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, while we're at this part of the document, can you tell us, if you know, what the handwriting in the circle indicates towards the bottom of the document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I've just explained. Underneath, it says: "Done in two copies." That's a mistake already. And then it was cc'd to these units, number 1, 1 times 1, the Security Administration of the General Staff. That's what's written in the document. Then the next one, 1 times Security Organ of the General Staff of the army, Kakanj, dash, and I don't see the rest, what it says, and then 1 times, and then there's a circle. This would mean that this document went to the command post of the Security Organ of the General Staff in Kakanj. Further on, it says -- I don't see the rest, but I see that it's the 3rd.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, if my colleagues from the OTP can ensure adequate translations into English in situations like this one. To see that a circle is made, you see, can a circle be placed in the English version too? Now the witness is explaining the relevancy of the fact that number 2 has been circled in the Bosnian version, and I don't see any circle like that in the English version.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We've made a note of that, Your Honours, and we'll seek to have this document revised.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I note the time. Before I turn to the next document, perhaps we could take the recess at this point in time, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis. We'll take a break and come back at quarter to 11.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. If the witness can now be shown Exhibit 858. Exhibit 858, please. If we could go to page 2 in the English and if we could get the full-screen version in the Bosnian, please. Page 2 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, can you tell us who signed this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I did.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, who drafted the document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Ganibegovic, Ibrahim.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I know that we will have this document corrected as well. Again, at the bottom in the list to which this document apparently was submitted there's a circle. Can you tell us what that represents and where this copy of this document was sent to, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This means that this secondary document which provides information, one copy of it was sent to the security organ of the army's General Staff in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I just ask a question here. Sir, does it mean that these other addressees who are not circled, does it mean it was not sent to them, the GS ARBiH UB, and the OB IKM Orahovo and the others?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If you look at this document, you can see that it's circled. You can see it was sent to the army's General Staff in Kakanj, which again implies --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Sorry, sir. I understand that. I'm talking about those that are not circled. Does it mean it was not sent to those who are not circled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When this information was written, it was decided, and that was the practice, that it should be forwarded to the organs as written here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Excuse me, sir. I must stop you. We're trying to get as short answers as possible. Was this document not sent to the addressees who are not circled?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document, what was circled means that only this organ received it. Another document was received by the Security Administration, General Staff of the Army of BH, and the first one, that was circled, and the rest was not, which means that it was sent then. The answer to the question about whether it was sent to these other organs, you can establish that if you look at the documents, if you look at the incoming registers.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm sorry, you're not answering my question. You know, I'm trying to understand the significance of the circling, sir. This document is addressed to several addressees, one, two, three, four, five. Only one is circled. Now, you've told us that the significance of the circle is that it was sent to that person who is circled. My question is, and you can answer it by saying either "yes" or "no," does this mean that those were sent to those who were not circled? That's a very simple question. It doesn't need a long explanation.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know that, but what is being shown to me, based on what is circled here, one could say that it was not sent to any of the other organs mentioned here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could now go back to page 1 in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, I'd like to focus your attention, please, on the second paragraph, and I have a very simple question for you. And this concerns the last sentence of the second paragraph. It states: "The security organ conducted the interview in the presence of the 35th Division intelligence officer in order to obtain intelligence and security-related information about the enemy." The interview that's referred to, Mr. Alihodzic, do you have any knowledge as to who conducted this interview, the person or persons who conducted this interview?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: As for the first and last name, I don't know who conducted this interview. It was conducted by one of the operatives of the security organ of the 35th Division of the ground forces based in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please go to document or Exhibit 859. I would ask if we go to the second page in Bosnian and the fourth page in English, please. I'm sorry, it should be the third page in Bosnian, and the bottom of that page in English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, we'll ask this document be revised to indicate the handwritten circle on the bottom of the document, but, sir, can you tell us whose signature this is, and who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This is my signature on this information. Who wrote this, it's not identifiable, apart from the letter "E." I assume -- I assume that this might have been -- I can't even assume. I apologise. No assumption. I thought Major Ancic at first, but then I couldn't. The initial is "E". I can't remember the first and last name of the typist who did this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could then please go back to the first page of the document in both languages.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And again, sir, I would refer your attention to the first paragraph of this document that again makes reference to: "Interview of the captured aggressor soldiers by the 35th Division Military Security Service organ." And I would ask you, sir, if you recall or have any knowledge as to who, within the 35th Division Military Security Service organ, conducted the interview with these three individuals.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Judging by the first and last names, I don't know who conducted the interview.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, sir, any additional specifics concerning the three individuals who were captured and whose names appear on this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Aside from what I can actually see, what I'm looking at, this information being shown, and now this reminds me -- takes me back to a time when this was all happening, I can't remember any other details, and it's not entirely certain that I can even remember this, to additionally recognate my memories, persons, other information, and knowledge.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that document be put away. I would ask the witness be shown PT01872. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, please leave the document on screen. I'm extremely sorry to go back to the issue of the circle, but I'd like to know the following, Witness: To your knowledge, the stamp that we see at the top, is that the stamp of the organ that received the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, I can read what the stamp contains: "Republic of Bosnia and Herzegovina, General Staff of the Army, Administration of the Military Security Service," number such-and-such, the date being what it is, the 28th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] According to you, does that correspond to the addressee that had a circle affixed to it? Could we show the bottom part of the document where we have the list of addressees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's what it says, "Security Administration, General Staff of the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Would I be mistaken if I said that the circle around the "1" next to the addressee was affixed by the addressee who received the document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It's exactly the opposite. The circling was executed by whichever organ put together this information, this being the security organ of the 3rd Corps, and they would circle number 1, the first document, to be sent there, and then expediting the General Staff, Kakanj, on the other document, same substance, same signature. And then the third, the fourth, and so on and so forth. How many people, how many organs that were sent this, that's how many copies the information was reproduced in. Individually, on each single sheet of paper, you could circle one organ, that being the organ that the information was forwarded to.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you for this clarification; that is to say, that in this particular document, this circle around just one of the addressees does not mean that the document was sent just to this one?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, that's right. This document that was circled once, one time, security organ of the General Staff of the army in Kakanj, means that it certainly went to the command post in Kakanj, the command post in Kakanj. Now, that is the problem. If you look at the header of the document at the top of the document, you asked me about that stamp, the square stamp. You asked me what it says. Judging by that, if you look at that, it follows that the document went to Sarajevo, the Security Administration of the General Staff of the Army in Sarajevo, and that was not the case, which means that the security organ in Sarajevo of the Security Administration had this stamp -- such a stamp, and the security organ in Kakanj had the same stamp. That causes an impossibility, in terms of properly identifying the document, in terms of who received it, if we look at the stamp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I just wanted to make sure that the other copies that we do not have here, that the other copies sent to the organs listed here would have been circled depending on the organ they were sent to?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That's right, Your Honour, just that organ.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I just heard that you said this document was sent to everyone. The witness never said that, if I may just notice for the record. I heard you say that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you, Madam Vidovic. Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honours. I would ask now that the witness be shown PT01871. PT01871.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, do you see the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, but it is difficult to take it all in.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, who produced this document or who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we see the heading of the English version, please. Thank you. I'm sorry to interrupt, Mr. Mundis, but can I get confirmation of the date as it appears on the Bosnian version, of the date of this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, do you see the date of this document, please, and can you tell us what that date is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Zenica, the 20th, possibly the 28th of November, 1994. The 20th or possibly the 28th.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, can you tell us who drafted this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Judging by the initials, Mr. Mehmed Siljak, "MS" with a diacritic, Mehmed Siljak.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, who was Mr. Mehmed Siljak?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: He was an operative, an analyst with the Military Security Department of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, sir, based on the markings on this document, where this document was sent?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, things being what they are, it wasn't sent anywhere, because nothing is circled. What we said before, what we discussed. Logically, this document could only have remained with the Military Security Department of the 3rd Corps, but that's not necessarily what it means. I don't think there's a clear-cut answer to this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see the stamp below your type-signed name? And if you do see that stamp, can you tell us what that stamp says or what that stamp indicates?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The stamp says: "Main Staff of the Armed Forces, Security Administration," in the Latin script, and in the Cyrillic, the same thing, and the date, the 21st of November, 1994.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Turning, sir, to the contents of the document, can you tell us what is being reported in this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: It's difficult to read because the Bosnian is very difficult to see. Paragraph 1 mentions the arrival of the El Mujahedin unit, that's what it says, in Livade village.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me just interrupt you there, sir. Do you know how Mr. Mehmed Siljak came to draft this document concerning the arrival of the El Mujahedin unit in Livade village?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Given the fact that this is a primary document, and Mehmed Siljak as the security organ of the 3rd Corps, the Military Security Department went to the security organ of the 35th Division or, rather, this is OG Bosnia [as interpreted], and made a note on the application of methods and work of the security organ, which it forwarded to the Military Security Department. That's one way. The other way could have been this: The security organ of OG Bosnia [as interpreted] used the regular format for Q and A and for reporting within the Military Security Service, and made a report that was received by the Corps or, rather, by the security department of the 3rd Corps, and in the absence of any possibility to gain insight into this primary document, I can't say with any certainty whether this is an official note or a report, but it was either of these two that reached the Security Service of the 3rd Corps in a written form, which was then used as a basis for this information that you see here.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We'd ask that this document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I would like to see the English translation of the handwritten remarks before we do that. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Perhaps let me ask a follow-up question concerning that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you know whose handwriting appears on the top of this document? There appears to be two different handwritings. Do you recognise either, or both, or neither of those handwriting exemplars?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I see two different samples, but I can't confirm who they belong to because I don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much. We'd ask the document be admitted into evidence, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 932.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask that the witness now be shown the document marked PT02064. PT02064, please. And if we could please see the entire document in Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you recognise this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This document is a report or information. It's a primary document in nature, to the Military Security Service on the 10th of May, 1995. If you could please pull it up for the initials so that we can see who drafted it.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Go to page 2 in Bosnia and page 3 in English, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This information was put together by Osman Vlajcic. I signed it, although there is no signature, but I think the document must be identical. And that's as far as I can see. You can't see who it was delivered to, but there are some markings there, Security Administration, counter-intelligence section of the 3rd Corps, the analysis sector of the 3rd Corps. So that's where the document should be found.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, to the left, above the initials of Mr. Vlajcic and the typist, we see the following words written: "Source: Reliable. Information: True." Can you explain to us what that means?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This is lack of training on the part of the security organ who wrote this information. Absence of training or insufficient training, because in the existing terminology used by the Military Security Service, a source is a person who works in parallel to the Military Security Service. In their working methodology, this would imply that the security organ had different ways open to it, in terms of obtaining such intelligence. If, for example, a degree of truthfulness was ascertained, then you could speak of an associate or an informer of the Military Security Service. No sources were evaluated in that sense, but I know who the operative officer is behind this. I know whose methodology this is. I recognise the terminology. This is Osman Vlajcic, a retired official of the State Security Service, and this would be in the domain of their own evaluations of persons who they worked with, in the operative sense, and obtained information from. This would mean that he's claiming that the source of this particular piece of information is reliable and the actual information is accurate.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, during the period 1995, when you were the assistant commander for security in the 3rd Corps, to whom did Mr. Vlajcic report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: To me.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can we please go back to page 1 of both versions of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any recollection or knowledge as to how Mr. Vlajcic came upon the information that is set forth in this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: He resorted to terminological declarations, as I've explained before, and this wasn't something that was not typical of the Military Security Service. I can assume that --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me interrupt you, sir, if I may. My question, simply, is: Do you know how Mr. Vlajcic obtained the information contained in this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's what I'm trying to say. That was the next step that I was taking. This is about the application of means and methods of work of the Military Security Service. One of these methods was secret recordings that were made. I associate that method with what the first sentence says, "an entirely reliable source." I'm making a link there.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And what do you mean, sir, by: "One of these methods was secret recordings that were made"? Can you elaborate on that sentence, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Certainly. The security organ of the Service of Military Security, regardless of level of organisation or establishment structure from battalion, brigade, division, corps, the Administration of Military Security had the powers of the Military Security Service, meaning certain rights that they could exercise. And also within the rules of service of the organs of the military police, the methods and ways in which the military security should work were prescribed as well. One of the methods was personal observations of the authorised official, interviews, working with contacts, secret intercepts, listening to intercepts, intercepting mail and so on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Alihodzic. The Prosecution would ask this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit 933.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask the witness now be shown the document marked PT02107. PT02107, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, do you see the document on the screen in front of you, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us what this document is, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This is a piece of information, a secondary document -- no, sorry, a primary document. I beg your pardon. It's a secondary document; that is to say, it was created at the second level.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us -- if we could go to page 2, please, in the English. Can you tell us, sir, who drafted this document and on whose authority the document was drafted?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: It was drafted with my approval. That's the way I see it. As for how I understood this document, I would need to see the primary document, where I initialled it by the heading, where I said everything that should be done in relation to this document. So I really cannot say on the basis of this. It's Ganibegovic, Ibrahim, who drafted it, and I signed it. It says here "Unsigned," but probably there is a piece of information that was signed.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we can go back to page 1 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you have any recollection of the information that's being reported in this document?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we turn to page 2 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you remember these incidents that are reported in this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: If I were not to be looking at this document, I would remember the content of this document or, rather, the action that had been taken at the time, because this did cause some attention on my part. This is just jogging my memory, in terms of the form in which it was written.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you remember anything -- you just told us, sir, that this: "This did cause some attention on my part," and I'm wondering if you could elaborate upon that, if you could tell us what you mean by that.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, the attention was due to the fact that this had to do with desecration of tombs. But generally speaking, may I say something about this document? There is something here that differs from the standards of military security. We aspired for that, but we did not always manage to do that because of the level of education of our organs. It does not contain the way or method in which these data were obtained. Also, the data referred to here in this information should have been dealt with in a different way. My recollection is that this action was taken, but at that time I could not, through the engagement of all the division organs, I could not ensure the documentation of these persons, in terms of their affiliation with the Mujahedin Detachment. You see, it says here in the first paragraph: "Members of the detachment," and in the third and fourth he uses the word "El Mujahedin" under quotation marks. So the detachment was unequivocal there, and my thoughts and the entire operational investigation of the developments meant that we could not establish whether it was done by someone from the detachment or some of the Mujahedin who were not within that detachment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if my colleague, the Prosecutor, can explain, it's a question of translation. Page 46, line 9, the witness is now talking about the first part of the document where El Mujahid is referred to, and then he starts talking about Mujahedin. However, it is the word "El Mujahedin" that is entered into the transcript, and the witness is making a distinction.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I think that's clear from the transcript, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But, sir, when you make this distinction between El Mujahedin unit and Mujahedin, are you quoting from the document that's on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I see that precisely in the document, that that is the way it's represented there. In essence, these are two different things. The first means a member of the detachment El Mujahedin, and the second statement has to do with a particular individual being a Mujahedin, which does not mean that this person belongs to the detachment of El Mujahedin.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And let me ask you that, sir, because that raises an interesting point, the distinction between El Mujahedin unit and Mujahedin as reflected in this document. What steps, if any, did you take to determine whether the actions described in this document were attributable to the El Mujahedin unit?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Without looking at this document, I stated that I recall this incident because it attracted my attention. I certainly distinguish between members of the detachment and Mujahedins, because a Mujahid, a Mujahedin, in terminology could have meant any --

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But my question, sir, was a slightly different one. I understand the distinction in the terminology. My question is: Based on this report that talks about members of the El Mujahedin unit, it says at the top of page 2 in the English, in the first page obviously in the Bosnian: "Immediately after taking over the trenches, the El Mujahedin members started demolishing tombstones in the cemetery." And my question to you is: What steps, if any, did you take, as the assistant commander for security of the 3rd Corps, to ascertain who had desecrated this cemetery?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: You see, these measures that were taken by the Military Security Service. Now we're talking about measures that I took. The Military Security Service, on the basis of initial knowledge, initial knowledge, engaged itself in documenting this case. These measures - yet again, due to the lack of documents concerned and the confirmation of my statement, let me be 100 per cent convincing - were directed at the following: To reconstruct or, rather, carry an on-site investigation. I remember that this incident was documented. There must be a cassette somewhere as well. However, this meant other measures, too; establishing the persons who are participants in these events and conducting interviews in order to document the incident. Those are the measures that were taken by the Military Security Service.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, if I may, could you look at the last paragraph of this document and tell us whether this expression, in English, "El Mujahedin unit," one meant the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could you explain to us why it is said here that one should take all the necessary measures as regards these soldiers of the El Mujahedin Detachment if, as you have told us, you didn't acknowledge that these were the members of this particular detachment who had committed these crimes or this crime?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, the answer to that question reflects the level of education and training on the part of the security organ of that division. If he had been trained enough, he would not have made a mistake in the second paragraph, referring to the detachment and to El Mujahedins. He considers this to be a conclusion, and again he is in a position to claim or, rather -- rather say that this was done by the El Mujahedin Detachment. That is why he is writing it there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But, sir, this document goes under your signature. Therefore, you should correct it. If his level of education causes him to make such mistakes, we expect that you should correct them before you sign the document. At this time now, as we are talking, we don't attribute this document to that person, we attribute it to you, the signatory, and therefore any mistakes in here must be explained by you. You can't explain them by referring to the level of education of the draftsman. What steps did you take, sir, to correct that problem, that mistake?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Behind this document, behind this piece of information, I assume there are other documents as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed, but what did you do to correct the mistake on this document, not the mistake behind the document, on this paragraph?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] In terms of correcting the mistake on this document, I can say that I didn't do anything, because that would mean that I would leave all my principal work and tasks and that I go to Zavidovici, which is 50 kilometres away, to train security organs. And in the chain of tasks -- well, I don't want to preempt matters, but I don't know where, on this ladder, such tasks were, in terms of our priorities. But the important thing is that the service registered even the most minor points. They did not hide anything from themselves and others, so everything could be further observed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can I be clear, understand what you're saying? Do I understand you to say that the person who drafted the document for you to sign sits 50 kilometres away from you, sat at that time 50 kilometres away from you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The person who drafted this document sat in the Command, in the building where I was.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: What has 50 kilometres got to do with your answer or with the question that I've put to you?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, it has to do with what I'm saying right now. I mean, this document was created on the basis of a report or a note of the security organ of the 35th Division, who was in Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You understand the distinction between the Mujahedin and El Mujahedin Detachment. When the man in your office drafts the document and writes this last paragraph and says to you, "You must sign that because of the events that have happened," you're going to make sure that proper discipline is maintained within the El Mujahedin unit, when in fact, according to you, it is Mujahedin, why do you allow yourself to sign the document in that form? You've just answered a question to Judge here now. You have no answer?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no answer, but I can only add that this is one of the 110 documents that --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: If you don't have an answer, thank you so much. Mr. Mundis, you can continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. We'd ask this document be admitted into evidence, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 934.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I'd ask that the witness now be shown the document that's marked PT02340. PT02340.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, do you see this document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, please - and perhaps we go to page 2 in English - who signed this document, sir, and who was the drafter of this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I signed the document, and it was drafted by Mr. Osman Vlajcic. And the document was sent, I'd say that straight away, to the Security Department of the General Staff in Kakanj.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, if we could go back to page 1 in English, please, sir, do you see in the very first line of this document it states: "Through a completely reliable source, we learned about the contact that Isaa from the El Mujahedin unit had with E. Muad from Rijadh, Saudi Arabia." Do you see that, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Do you recall, Mr. Alihodzic, or can you tell us, if you know, how it is that Mr. Vlajcic came upon the information that is contained in this report?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vlajcic obtained these results by applying the method of secretly listening in on conversations.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. We would ask that this document be admitted, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 935.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I would ask the witness now be shown Exhibit 773. Exhibit 773, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, do you see this document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you perhaps tell us, sir, at the top, in the center of the document, there's some handwriting under the initials "KOO," do you see that handwriting, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I can't see the "KOO." I don't know where you see that. Oh, this thing up here, yes, yes. The handwritten part, yes, I see that.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Whose handwriting is that, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That is my handwriting.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And can you tell us, Mr. Alihodzic, who was this handwriting directed to? In other words, were you asking someone or directing someone to do something, and if so, who?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I wrote in hand, in terms of this document, that it came to the Corps, to the head of the counter-intelligence organ, Mr. Osman Vlajcic, and I gave him the task to check this person, whether he was a member, and to give him permission to get a travelling document in order to be given medical treatment abroad, as stated in this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And if we could please scroll on the Bosnian version to the far right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, we see some additional handwriting -- other side, please. We see some other handwriting in the top right corner of this document. Do you recognise whose handwriting that is?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I cannot recognise the handwriting at this very moment, but I assume it's Osman who checked things with the Personnel Service at the Command of the 3rd Corps, and he established that this person was in that unit, in the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Sir, when you say you assume it's Osman, can you please tell us his full name?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Osman Vlajcic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you, sir. Now, this document -- perhaps if we could see the full version of the document in both languages. This document, sir, relates to an individual by the name of Izudin Besic; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And I take it, sir, from that name, Mr. Besic is a Bosniak.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Can you tell us, sir, the procedure that was undertaken when you received a document such as this, in terms of obtaining passports for foreign travel? What steps, if any, did the Security Department of the 3rd Corps take upon receiving such documents?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: There's several questions there, but allow me to say this, ultimately: This is the first document that came to the Corps, the 3rd Corps, in this form. Because he says here permission is sought to obtain a passport, well, maybe something else appeared, too, but we're looking at this now. However, that is not practice. The 3rd Corps did not issue passports. This is quite unclear. There's a question mark here. I, myself, do not have an answer, why this document appeared. I can assume that a soldier was sick and that perhaps certain problems were encountered, in terms of the procedure of obtaining a passport, but it was the State Security Service or, rather, the appropriate organ in the State Security Service that issued passports, and, inter alia, a document was required. When this person addresses them, then this corresponding organ from the State Security Service would turn to us, and we would give them a certificate once a check had been made in the Personnel Department as to whether a certain person is a member or not. So the question really is how this document appeared in the first place. I have no answer to that. But the procedure with regard to issuing passports was quite different. Another thing I'm wondering about in relation to this document, this stamp of the Detachment El Mujahedin, I'm convinced, because this is was under the Corps to have stamps made, and this stamp was prescribed, in terms of form, through a certain order. It could not have had this kind of content or this kind of image.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me ask you, though, sir, because you just told us when -- and this is on lines 19 through 22 of page 54: "When this person addresses them, then this corresponding organ from the State Security Service would turn to us ..." This document you see on the screen before you, sir, is not from the State Security Service, is it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and it's abnormal that it should turn up with the security organ, but I can't remember why it turned up there. And then I go into the procedure of thinking about this, whether there was a misunderstanding somewhere along the line, or perhaps the need to speed things up so that passports were issued more expeditiously.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me -- perhaps there's some confusion. Are you telling us, sir, that this document that we see on the screen in front of us came from the State Security Service?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: No. It stems from the El Mujahedin Detachment, addressed to the Military Security Department -- Services Department of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The department that you headed during this time period of this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: If we could please now turn to Exhibit 772. Exhibit 772.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, do you recognise the document on the screen in front of you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And whose signature appears on this document, sir? And if we could go to page 2 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I see my signature.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: And, sir, what was the purpose of this document? And we can go back to page 1 in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The purpose of this document was to grant approval for passports to be issued. In the upper left-hand corner, you see, and there is a document they produced being invoked, and that's probably the previous document, in terms of the number, and we say that we, in connection with the document, we are hereby informing them that we agree that a member of their unit, Izudin Besic, and then I can't see what it says, be issued a passport.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Could we please zoom in on the top half of this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I appreciate, Mr. Alihodzic, that this is not a very good copy. If we could then scroll over to the right, please. Can you see to whom this document is addressed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The commander of the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you. We'll endeavor to get the English translation of this document revised.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Now, sir, let me ask you this: Do you recall receiving one such request concerning checks for purposes of issuing of passports, or was there more than one such request? And I'm referring specifically to requests from the El Mujahedin Detachment.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I said this was unusual and this was not the prescribed procedure or behaviour, in terms of these problems, I mean, issuing documents. There was an entirely different procedure in place, entirely different.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: But my question, sir, was: Was this the only such request you received from the El Mujahedin Detachment or did you remember or do you remember receiving similar requests from that detachment during the period of time that you were the assistant commander for security in the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I can assure you categorically that this is one document, and I don't think that another can turn up about granting approval, in terms of passports being issued. I don't know how this ever appeared. I don't know how my signature is there. I can assume -- I can speculate maybe it's about the ill health of that particular soldier, and probably there was some obstacle to be overcome in connection with the appropriate state organ. And then due to haste, you know, overcoming obstacles, that sort of thing, the prescribed time for the passport to be issued, maybe this was a way of expediting the procedure in terms of having the passport issued. I can only assume that in this case, but I can't remember any other cases such as this one.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Let me put a more direct question to you, sir. Do you ever remember whether there were similar requests concerning foreign members of the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I can't, I can't remember, but requests, I know. We're talking about a document that is outside procedure, requests for documents to be issued according to the established procedure by members of the El Mujahid Detachment, well, foreigners, Afro-Asians, well, yeah, those were made, because that's what it says here, this statement that you can read in the last paragraph of this document, how these documents should be handled, what are the responsibilities of the individual in question, what are the responsibilities of the unit, and so on and so forth. So this cooperation addressing the State Security Service or, rather, the appropriate organ for public documents, for passports, that sort of thing, to us what that meant is we were exercising control over the presence of military personnel in Bosnia. Otherwise, they could have bypassed us without that request, and then the soldiers would have been able to travel unhampered and maybe something worse would have happened than what actually happened, and that's why it was not within the authority of the Military Security Service to grant any approvals to members of the army without our consent, and the consent implied that the soldier would go and speak to his commander, to his unit, about a certain problem, "Sir, Commander, I'm sick, I have to go and receive treatment," and there are conventions that the commander grants or refuses this, and he gives the green light for this soldier to go to the Security Administration or whatever and get the appropriate papers issued.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, I appreciate the difficulties here, particularly when we're working in different languages, but let me ask you this question one last time, sir. Do you remember receiving any requests from the El Mujahedin Detachment concerning requests for approval, in terms of issuing passports? And this can be answered either "yes," "no," "I don't know," "I don't remember."

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I know that passports were issued to members of the detachment, the El Mujahedin Detachment, but not in the procedure of the Military Security Service.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: My question, sir, is not whether the Military Security Service or the 3rd Corps or the army issued the passports. My question is whether you remember receiving any requests from the El Mujahedin Detachment seeking approval for the issuance of passports to foreign members of that detachment. "Yes," "no," "I don't know," "I don't remember"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Thank you very much, sir. The Prosecution has no further questions for the witness at this time, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you. Before the document gets off the screen, I would just like to see the end of the document in the English, please. Is this the end of the document in English? Thank you very much. Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I don't think it would be a meaningful exercise to start now, because the document will take some time appearing on our screens and until -- I think it's better to have the break now, if I could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Madam Vidovic. We'll then take a break and come back at half past 12.00. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Alihodzic.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'll be examining you on behalf of General Delic's Defence. Most of my answers -- most of my questions can be answered with a straight "yes" or "no." I have many questions. It is vital that we finish today because of your health concerns. If there is any need for you to explain in greater detail, I'll be glad to allow you to do just that, but, please, whenever you can, keep it down to a straightforward "yes" or "no." That is the procedure that cross-examination, as such, entails. Also, please speak as slowly as possible. Each time after I finish my question, please make a pause before you start your answer so that everything gets recorded. Do you understand?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Prosecutor asked you some questions about documents that describe certain procedures to do with POWs. I'll be asking you about that, too. First of all, you will agree with me, won't you, that the Corps SVB received copies of the international legal conventions known as the Geneva Conventions that, among other things, talk about the treatment of POWs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: If that's a question, yes, I do remember that, and I know that well, that the conventions existed. They came from the level of the General Staff of the BH Army, the objective being to distribute them from the lowest units in the General Staff, subordinate units to the General Staff, and then these units were supposed to forward this down the chain of command to the lowest-ranking units, and even the soldiers on the ground had to be familiar with these.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. So you forwarded these conventions to the lower-ranking units, did you not?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Security Administration submitted instructions as far as the treatment of POWs was concerned; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that sort of document, too, and other documents that were like it. This was an effort, at a time when the army was being established, to carry out some essential tasks; among other things, to use this method also to better train organs of the Military Security.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Mr. Alihodzic. These explanations are extremely helpful, but I simply don't have enough time. Please focus, if you can, on my questions, "yes" or "no" whenever possible, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Instructions on how POWs were to be treated, this was also something that you sent along down the chain of command to lower-ranking units; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about the combat orders of the 3rd Corps, did they not regulate exactly how POWs were to be treated in the portion of the document that had to do with security; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The commands of these lower-ranking units, subordinate units, divisions and brigades, knew exactly what their responsibilities were and what they were supposed to do when coming into contact with POWs; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Security Administration requested that reports be submitted on information to do with POWs; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we now please have Exhibit 580.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were shown this exhibit today by the OTP. Mr. Alihodzic, let's not try -- let's try not to spend too much time on this. This is a document produced by the 3rd Corps, the Security Service Department. The date is the 22nd of July, 1995. Results of offensive activities in the area of responsibility of the 35th Division. Today, you saw this document, and you confirmed that this was your signature. If we could please pull it up a little.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you remember that it was in relation to this document that we had a discussion as to who it was delivered to; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Mr. Alihodzic, can you just look at the lower half of the document. It can be seen in English as well. You agree that just about where it says "delivered" and above the initials, we see this: "Produced in duplicate"; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And in the document, there are a total of four addressees mentioned; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. In other words, we have two copies being made of this document. Whenever this is the case, one of these must always remain in the archive of your service; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, just one of these two documents could have been delivered to someone who was about in the field; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: In the -- the latter half of the document, where it says "delivered" and then circled, this certainly went to the Security Administration, the command post that it had in Kakanj, I think.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. So two copies were made of this, and it could not possibly have been delivered to four addressees, could it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I would need documents -- I would need some hard evidence to confirm that, but that is what the logic of this document seems to imply.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, if you only have a mere two copies made of a certain document, what does that mean, in terms of who it can be sent to and how many addressees?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, that's what I'm trying to say. Two copies were made. That's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So how could it possibly have been forwarded to four different addressees if there were only two copies to begin with?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, in order to ascertain that -- well, based on this, obviously, this would have been impossible, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, sir, I just want you to keep this date in mind, regardless of whether it was delivered to Sarajevo or Kakanj. But, first of all, I want you to look at the beginning of this document. Could we please take the English back to page 1. You see this marking here. This is being delivered to the General Staff in Kakanj by courier. You saw that, didn't you? Is there anything here to indicate that the document was encrypted before it was sent anywhere else?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The document, the way it's shown, there is nothing to confirm that it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In an encrypted form, you mean?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right. There is absolutely nothing to indicate that it was sent.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Please just try to keep the date in mind, and now please focus on the portion of the document that states that the El Mujahedin Detachment were allowing no access. You will remember that this is something that the document states, right, no access to POWs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's what it says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You saw the same thing being stated in E364, another document that the Prosecutor was showing you today, which also stated that the El Mujahedin were barring access to POWs. You remember looking at another document that said the same thing; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do remember.
