utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Your Honours, can we just look at this now, paragraph 2, second sentence of paragraph 2. It reads: "We have no information about the number of aggressor soldiers who were wounded and killed. About 50 aggressor soldiers were taken prisoner, 11 of them Muslims." Let me ask you something about this figure, 50 members of the Republika Srpska Army. Did you ever receive any confirmation whatsoever of what is stated here, to the fact that the El Mujahedin, in the month of July, took 50 prisoners?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: What I'm saying is this: This is a secondary document. It was drafted based on another primary document which had arrived there as a report or a note on work methodology and the application of appropriate methods. In terms of its format, it was initial information. We had no right to hold anything like that back. We just informed other people. And our task, in relation to this particular piece of information and other information - I'm just trying to use some time here to avoid commenting later - to carry out operative investigations, to verify the authenticity and reliability of any such information. The same applies to this. Right away, we see here in these documents, there's two doctors and one nurse. I know that we never actually received confirmation that there was two doctors and one nurse. I think there was a doctor and a nurse actually.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, slow down. The interpreter is struggling very hard to keep pace with you, sir. Can you just slow down so that he can interpret?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, Your Honour. What I'm trying to say here is this: There will be final information about the number of prisoners, but this figure here was never confirmed, and that much is certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, you will remember that the Prosecutor today showed you E858, dated the 23rd of July, in which you also informed the Security Administration, be it the one in Kakanj or the one in Sarajevo, no matter, about POWs. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These same POWs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And now, Your Honours, could we please put this document away. I would like the witness to look at 859 now, Exhibit 859.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I've seen it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, it's another document that you saw today.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let's have another look. The date is the 25th of July, 1995, and --

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It talks about the results of interviews conducted with captured aggressor soldiers. I think that today you confirmed that what we can see on this document is your signature. Right? I don't think there's any need to go back to that. Right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I do know that, because there are other versions of the same document, this same document, but other versions, different headers, details that ultimately don't really matter.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fair enough. Judging by the stamp, the document was received on the 28th of July, 1996 -- 1995. My apologies, 1995.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now could you please read the first sentence of this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: "The security organs of the Military Security Service of the 35th Division conducted interviews with captured aggressor soldiers and reached the following conclusions and information: "The interview was conducted with:" And then a list of persons who were interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, there is no way the interpreters can possibly keep up with you. Slow down, please, if you can. Just one thing. Do you agree that this document was produced as a result of interviews conducted by organs of the Military Security Service of the 35th Division with captured aggressor soldiers?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right. There was no other way, there was no other possibility for a document like this to come about.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Let me remind you of this now. You remember looking at two other documents, previous documents. I showed you one and the Prosecutor showed you another, documents stating that the El Mujahedin Detachment were barring access to POWs, including these three persons mentioned here, Sikanic; Trivicevic, Velibor; and Guljevati, Igor. You remember that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, please, let's take this slowly. Can you look at these pages slowly, one by one, page 1 to begin with?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Page 2 now, please, both languages. Can we move on to the next page, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, we had two documents in which information was forwarded to you, which you then passed along, to the effect that the El Mujahedin Detachment were barring access to POWs. Do you agree that what this document shows is this: The Military Security Service or, rather, its organ, in actual fact, on the 25th of July, 1995, had, in fact, access to these POWs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it had access to POWs in this particular situation and to these particular persons who they interviewed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes. In other words, bearing in mind -- do you agree that what we can see here is a number of details that they obtained through those interviews?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, of course I agree with that. Yes, that's what the interviews were for. That's why they were conducted, to collect intelligence; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I know, Mr. Alihodzic, but, please, keep your answers brief, to the extent that you can, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Sure.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So on the face of this document, there is no mention whatsoever of the fact that these people were encountering any further problems; the 35th Division is no longer reporting about the fact that the El Mujahid Detachment were barring access; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, they are not even informing you, through this document, that they're holding them, right, in this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, this document also in this way does not inform you about any kind of inhumane treatment towards prisoners of war; are you right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: You are right, Madam.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, did you ever receive any information about inhumane treatment of prisoners of war by this detachment? I'm referring to these prisoners from the month of July.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Had you had such information, you would have recorded it; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: By all means.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would have certainly taken measures that you were duty-bound to take?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: By all means. This is a very serious matter and it requires the service to act.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Acting would mean carrying out an investigation from pre-criminal proceedings; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. This document can be put away. Your Honour, at this moment I'd like the witness to have a look at Exhibit 591.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'd like to ask you about a different topic that has to do with the El Mujahedin Detachment. Please have a look at this document. This is a document of the Security Department, dated the 22nd of April, 1995, and it refers to a list of members of the El Mujahedin unit. You mentioned lists today, lists of the unit. If you think that the document is not clear and that you cannot read it, we can give you a hard copy, if you wish. First of all, I want to ask you whether this is your signature.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Have you read the document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, I'm trying, but I cannot read it in its entirety.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You'll get a hard copy.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, do you agree that it refers to the order of the commander of the 3rd Corps to the El Mujahedin unit to stop taking soldiers in, foreigners and our citizens?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What is also asked is information about possible admissions that took place after the order of the corps commander?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The order was therefore in force at least on the 22nd of April, 1995, and if we look at the second paragraph of the document, it is obvious that the order was issued earlier. So now my question to you is: Do you remember -- since this is an important matter, can you remember when the order was issued banning further admissions into the El Mujahedin Detachment?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I didn't really understand you about this question. As for the date, I just see "the 22nd of April, 1995" here.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm going to read a paragraph out to you -- paragraph 2 to you now. It says, please: "If any new people were admitted, foreigners or Bosniaks, to this unit after the order of the 3rd Corps commander, please provide the data to the OSVB of the 3rd Corps."

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I understand.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This second paragraph that I just quoted from says that before this day, the 22nd of April, 1995, there was an order of the corps commander that had to do with the ban on admissions of new members into the unit. Can you remember when this order was issued or when you found out about it, if you can answer that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I cannot recall the date exactly, but I'm convinced and certain that these written orders by the Corps Command were there, because such matters did appear and they required a response. Even considerably earlier, in 1993, when I was a brigade commander, I know that I initiated that, this problem of the movement of soldiers from one unit to another.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Mr. Alihodzic. Your Honour, could this document please be removed, unless you have any questions. Could you now have a look at D721, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before that, I just want to ask you, Mr. Alihodzic: Do you agree that this document that you've seen just now indicates that the detachment did not have accurate records of foreigners who were members of the unit? You talked to us about that today.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: We did not have accurate records, we at the Personnel Department of the 3rd Corps, but the detachment of El Mujahedin did not have that, either, on the members of that detachment, that is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Mr. Alihodzic, do you agree -- well, you were not there, so you don't know what kind of records they had; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, do you agree -- actually, I want to ask you something different, that in the zone of responsibility of the 3rd Corps, there were a lot of Arabs who did not belong to the detachment at all?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: In the form of the existence of humanitarian organisations and other, how shall I put this, other forms of their stay were there, apart from the detachment, and there were quite a few, at that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you please have a look at this document now, D721. Do you agree that this is a document of the military security organ of the 319th Brigade, dated the 13th of July, 1995? And I would like to ask you to have a look at this stamp down here. Do you agree that this is a document that was received at the Department of the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps on the 13th of July, 1995?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Now, could the document please be scrolled up a bit so that the witness could see the beginning.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, as you compare your signatures, it seems that this is your signature below the handwritten note?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, in the upper part near the heading. That's my signature, and by the stamp is the signature of the security organ of the brigade.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Therefore, it's my conclusion that you had this document in your hands.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. It was sent to the counter-intelligence organ as well, and this was supposed to be a comprehensive piece of information.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Now, I hope -- well, you've had a look. Please read the document to yourself, to yourself. And for the transcript, I'm going to say that this is a report on contact with Zolja, a contact -- a person who was a contact. Do you see that the security organ of the 319th Brigade informs about his communication with a contact concerning the presence of Arabs in Zeljezno Polje?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I'm pleased to see this document. I can see that the security organ has knowledge of the matter and has learned how to do his work properly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that there is a number of Arabs in the area of Zeljezno Polje and there are others near Tesanj, that that's what the document says, and that perhaps it's the Arabs who desecrated the Catholic cemetery in Donja Golubinja, went there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that you learned that in the area of Zeljezno Polje and Tesanj, there are some Arabs who are active, and through the security organ of the 319th Brigade, you tried to gain some information about them?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the document also says that these people from Zeljezno Polje are desecrating Catholic graveyards?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I agree, because I do know about this area, anyway. It was indicative in other security problems. This is not the only one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, could this document please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 936.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could the witness please look at document D730 now, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you read the document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: It's hard to read. It would be a good thing --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We have a hard copy. For the record, I would like to say that this is information from the Security Service of the 3rd Corps, the 22nd of July, 1995, and the title of the document is: "Desecration of the Catholic cemetery - additional information."

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I'm pleased to see this document, too, because it shows continuity in the work of the military security organs.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: We see that Ibrahim Dzasim resides in the area of Zeljezno Polje?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: This person informed that Hamza and Dzafer desecrated the cemetery, and Hamza went to the Republic of Croatia. Then in the document you describe impeded cooperation with the Arabs. Nevertheless, according to this document, you do have knowledge that the Catholic cemetery was desecrated by Arabs who were active in Zeljezno Polje, not the El Mujahedin Detachment; isn't that right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that a lot of initial knowledge, in terms of which members of the detachment were blamed, this knowledge was changed later, to the effect that other Arabs were the perpetrators, as is the case here?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. I don't have time to go into all of that now, but it is a fact, what you are saying now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: As for this extended knowledge, you submitted that to the Security Administration as well; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In order for us here to get the right picture about the knowledge that the Security Administration had, we would have to have a look at the initial document you sent and then we would have to search the archives and find what your further knowledge was, so that we would obtain information as to what kind of knowledge, concerning a certain problem that you initially informed about, the Security Administration actually had?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right, that's right, because this initial information, if it did not have an end, if measures were not taken ultimately, then the security organs were duty-bound to document it further. It had to be confirmed and certain measures had to be taken either through the judiciary or through the RiK.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could this document please be assigned a number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It will be assigned a number. Let me just ask a question. I see, on the B/C/S version, that now the address -- three addressees are circled. What does that mean, Witness?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That means that this document was sent to the administration of the General Staff, to the forward command post, to the commander in Orahovac, and that it stayed in the archives of the Military Security Service of the 3rd Corps. And what was not encircled here, most probably, most probably, means that this document was sent to the forward command post in Kakanj by a courier. As for the ones with circles, were sent by Paket communication through the Communications Centre.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we just have a look --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Just a second. I'm still asking questions. Now, I thought you said this morning, in answer to a question by Judge Lattanzi, that the individual copy that you sent to a specific recipient is the one that is circled, not one common copy being circled for all of the recipients.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this must have been an omission on the part of the operations man who was putting the circles there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: It doesn't look like an omission. It looks like a commission, because now there are three circles instead of one, so something has been committed here, not omitted, sir.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really do not have an answer, Your Honour, except --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. Yes, except? Except what, sir?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, he did not say that. I did not hear the witness say "Osim."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Interpreters note, we did hear the witness say "osim," "except."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay, fine. Anyway, now, in response to a question by Madam Vidovic, you conceded that it is impossible to deliver four copies to four different recipients when there are only two copies. You remember that?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I remember.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Now, on this document, two copies were made. How do you get delivery to three people?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I really do not have an answer to that question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Yes, Madam Vidovic, you may proceed. The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 937.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And now about the information that you spoke of. For the most part, you submitted to the Security Administration information, regardless of whether we are talking about the Kakanj branch or the Sarajevo branch. You would obtain information based on operative knowledge and results; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, by all means. There was no other way. We used our operative work to obtain information, and we submitted this information as you suggested.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well. Information that was passed along to you from lower-ranking units would first be checked, and sometimes they would prove to be inaccurate; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. All the security organs stopped right there and did not pursue it any further, and then we had to prompt them to keep at it. They would forget. But they investigated, yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You would agree that sometimes rumour or hearsay would be included in what was termed "information"; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's how the whole war started, hearsay, rumours, propaganda, insinuations. This war, itself, was propaganda. The life of those, what shall I call them, individuals boiled down to just that and no more.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can the witness now please be shown Exhibit 764. Thank you. Just for the record, this is a document produced by the 3rd Corps Command, dated the 7th of July, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see what it says over there: "Code name: White Hen," and then there is what I believe is a stamp of the 3rd Corps Command, Security Service Department. You see that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Could we pull this document down a little, or pull it up, rather, so we can see the handwritten portion.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise anything there?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I recognise my handwriting. I signed this or, rather, addressed it to Redzo Camdzic for him to write up a report, and that he was to familiarise the division commander with this so that further measures could be ordered.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine, fine. So you made a suggestion to the commander of the 35th Division to take measures; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Look at this document now, please. It's about an incident in relation to a person named "Miro Huncek," an ethnic Croat. Please have a look, read it. Before I ask you anything about the incident itself, you agree that this is a typical textbook example of a primary document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Indeed. You can see that if you look at the header. The explanation implies that this is page 2, and page 1 was in a particular set format. It had the methodology shown right there and the equipment actually used. This is a document that was produced in the unit. If you look at the explanation, I put it somewhere in the identification and work methodology governing the work of the security organs of military security.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Let me ask you this: So this is a primary document. You used this to base another document on in order to spread information, and that is then a secondary document; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's exactly right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. You agree that this document says that members of the El Mujahedin unit arrived at the defence line and that not a single name is mentioned?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: About midway down the page, there is a reference to a Mujahedin asking about Miro, a Croat, "Where is he? I want to slit his throat." Can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I see that's what the document says.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then it goes on to state that the platoon commander gave a hint to Huncek to get out of there, which he did. And then please look at this: "News spread along the line that members of the El Mujahedin unit were on their way there and that they were in the mood to slit the throats of all non-Muslims there." And then it goes on to say: "After these incidents, rumours started to spread around town that there was no point in the Croats and the remaining Serbs going to the defence lines because allegedly members of the El Mujahedin unit would slit their throats, no matter if they were somewhere along the defence line or in their homes." All right. So you remember that, in essence, this document shows that a threat was made to a single Croat and certainly not -- this is a primary document, and what it shows is that this threat was made to a single Croat and not to all Croats and Serbs, not by any stretch of the imagination; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, you're 100 per cent right, but even this one, even that is very important. We believe this to be very important. That's why we wrote it up like this. That's why we looked into it. That's why we documented the whole incident. And then later there was operative work being done on this case, and then we investigated and so on and so forth.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right, thank you very much. So do you agree that even this one incident, this one threat being made to this one Croat, evolved in such a way that the rumour eventually spread that they were making threats to all Croats and Serbs; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's certainly true. I've no time here to explain the mission or the presence of international players in Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. This is propaganda, it's a war of propaganda, and this sort of propaganda would be spread across this area and other areas where they were staying at the time.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Another thing that happened is that rumours were circulating around town that threats were being made. That is the gist of this document; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. So you've just told us that you investigated this particular incident. What I'm trying to ask you is this --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Slow down, Madam Vidovic. Slow down, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Apologies.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you told us that you investigated this incident; right? Do you agree that you informed the Military Security Administration in Sarajevo about this investigation, wherever they happened to be, Military Security Administration, anyway?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't see based on this that this was actually done, but I'm certain that this was part of operative reporting, be it in the way of a summary, reports, or some other way of informing the Security Administration, whatever, 100 per cent certain.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. I'm pressing on with the documents. I'm trying to ask you the following thing: When you say --

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: It's this particular incident that I have in mind.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Please, Witness, I asked you and you said you investigated this incident, so I'm asking you: What about the results? Did you inform the Military Security Administration in Sarajevo about the results of this investigation?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, we must have passed that sort of information along to them. I'm certain of that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. All right, Your Honours, we can put this document away now, and we'll soon be looking at a different one. D648, please. For the record, this is an official note of the military security organ of the 35th Division, and the date is the 5th of July, 1995. This note was sent to the 3rd Corps Command, Military Security Department: Witness -- could this document be pulled down so we can see the bottom half of the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you agree that this document was received by the Security Service of the 3rd Corps?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, you can see that square stamp.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we go to page 2, please. Let me just see. While we're still on page 1, Your Honours -- all right, let's have a look.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fikret Skejic, was he a member of your service?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Indeed, he was.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the 35th Division?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, as a matter of fact, in the 35th Division. This implies this was in a functional sense.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: A member of the security service?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, a member of the Security Service of the 3rd Corps, or, rather, with certain involvement in the 35th Division; right?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please go back to page 1 now, page 1 of the Bosnian.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look at paragraph 2, and you will see a description there of that same incident to do with Miro Huncek. You see that; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. In order to save time, I'll quote a small portion of this document to you. It starts with: "On that occasion ..." "On that occasion, Miro told the El Mujahid member since the first day of aggression --" There's probably something missing: " ... who responded that he was not familiar with that incident and that if he had been properly informed, he would never have called him out and would never have requested that his throat be slit. Other non-Muslim persons were also threatened by this phenomenon." What I'm trying to ask you is this: Do you remember that this encounter between Miro Huncek and this unknown person, who appeared to be a member of the El Mujahid unit, was described in entirely different terms?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, no likeness at all, different as chalk and cheese.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If he'd known he was a member of the army, he would never have made any threats at all, would he?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I think the word was probably dropped, who had been a member of the BH Army from day 1, that was probably -- that qualification was dropped in the first version, the first account of this incident.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much. Your Honours, could we have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 938.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like you, sir, to look at two different documents now about the same subject matter. It's about information -- it's about work methods. E934, please, Exhibit -- Exhibit 934.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you agree that this is information produced by the 3rd Corps, Security Service Department. The date is the 26th of May, 1995, and this has to do with the tearing down grave slabs in Zavidovici Municipality, or tombstones. You commented on this document; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I remember that.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You were asked by the Judge, "Why did you not correct what you believed to be inaccurate in that document," and your answer was something along the lines -- well, you didn't finish answering. You said something along the lines of, "I had 150." You remember saying that? What, in actual fact, were you trying to say?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I wanted to say that there were 151, to be quite accurate, security organs who would each write up a single note, a one- or two-page note, or daily combat reports, a document running into 300 or so pages, and this took some time to read. And, above all, one needed to prioritise, and my priorities were foisted on me as a member of the army, as a private person who stood up to defend this country. And in the third place only, me, as the chief of the Military Security Service, and prioritise a certain task, and maybe at that point in time - and right now I don't have the operative documentation to say what on that particular day or over those days, was such a burning issue, what the situation happened to be across the area or in the area of responsibility of the Corps, specifically.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, Witness, do you agree that you issued orders for something that wasn't clear, to be further investigated; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: It's not that I issued orders. This was an ongoing commitment or responsibility. Whoever happened to see me from that security organ, the terminology, the methodology, they knew that they would get their knuckles rapped every time. They had to keep at it. They had to train themselves, because they had never been properly trained. They had not been properly educated to perform this sort of activity, which was a very serious kind of activity. But as a human being, I'm deeply satisfied that they managed to cover all the security problems, to put it that way, all the security problems that were later to be verified, confirmed, and so on and so forth. And this is something that I know about, and my evidence is that was precisely what we did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much, Witness. It is for your sake that I'm trying to wrap this up as quickly as possible, so, please, if you can keep your answers down to a simple "yes" or "no" whenever possible, or as brief as possible. The purpose of my question was the last thing you said. Okay, so this was initial information that you pursued, and then you passed such information along to the Military Security Administration; am I --

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, that's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Exhibit 666, please. The date is the 21st of June, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You see that; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Can we go to page 2 of this document, please. This is page 4 in the English.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you recognise the signature there, sir?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Is it yours?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Okay. Could we please go back to page 1 now.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you see what it says, the handwritten note: "Kakanj"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In the Bosnian as well as for the English -- oh, yeah, it's right there. Fine. Witness, the handwritten note right there, the handwritten note, you see that; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I see it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You recognise the handwriting, don't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: No, as a matter of fact, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Be that as it may, I'm going to ask you a question about the principle espoused here. It reads: "Make sure that information on this unit is not used outside the service." That's what it says. Can you please elucidate? What exactly does that note mean? What could that possibly mean? What sort of instructions are these?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This is a comment that was probably added by an organ or, rather, in the Security Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Yes, but what did it mean?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, what I should really do here is evaluate the need for this and other such information to not be communicated to members of the army outside the service, which doesn't mean that, in operative terms, this was not, in fact, done.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Does -- should I take your answer to mean that the instruction was really about these instructions or these, rather, details; this information was not to be used outside the service but just inside the service?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that precisely is the purpose. Someone was probably prompted. Maybe it wasn't about this particular case. Maybe there were other situations where attention needed to be drawn to this. Protecting, protecting, conspiratorially.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Okay. This is obviously what it's saying, that no information should be used anywhere outside the service, meaning the Military Security Service; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please put this document away, Your Honours. Could the witness please have a look at Exhibit 784. Could we now just show page 2 to the witness, the last page, that is, to establish whose signature is on the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is my signature.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we go back to page 1 of the Bosnian version.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, in relation to this document, I'm just interested in this note. You see, there is a date down there. First on the note -- on the document, it says: "Use only in operative work. Do not use the intelligence outside the service." And that is underlined?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that is what is written there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The date is the 23rd of June, 1995. Witness, do you recognise the initials down there? Do you know whose initials these are?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I really don't know whose initials these are, but it only could have been initialled by a person in the Security Administration.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that over here it also says: "Do not use intelligence outside the service"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Also, it says: "Use exclusively in operative work"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Such notes mean that this should not be submitted to anyone outside the Security Service?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that would mean that, until information is confirmed, extended and so on. But as for this document, it means that this commander was not familiar with it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Could this document please be removed now.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I want to just ask one or two questions. There's something a little surprising to me about this document. It was written on the 22nd of June. It was received at the General Staff, Military Security office, on the 24th. Somewhere in between, on the 23rd, a note is made on it. Now, unfortunately, the witness says he does not know who made this note, and it becomes important to know where it was on that date. Does it mean it went with this note from where it was being sent, the note of the 23rd?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, this document was written on the 22nd, and it means that it was sent on that day to the Security Administration. And, really, there is this illogical thing, that it was received on the 24th, and then this content referring to the 23rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: So it -- it couldn't have been sent on the 22nd if something was done on it on the 23rd, before it reached its destination. It can only mean that it was either sent -- it was written on the 22nd, and on the 23rd somebody made this note before it was sent off?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No, no, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: But your proposition is impossible, to suggest that it was sent on the 22nd and received on the 24th, and somewhere in between, somebody wrote on it, unless it was not sent in an envelope.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Please, could I just see the signature? Could the document be scrolled up a bit more?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, it's on the next page.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] See.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: That's your signature, sir?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, this is my signature. Now could you return the document back there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: And you don't know who made the handwritten note?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know who wrote that. Now, I do apologise. Just one more detail. Where those circles were put as to where the document was submitted, in order to try to answer, the lower left-hand corner, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go to it.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The lower left-hand corner, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No circle for addressees.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Unfortunately, yes. I am now reverting to logic. It seems logical that it was in an envelope and sent to the operations officer at the forward command post in Kakanj, that he received it, initialled it on the 23rd, and that subsequently he gave it to the man in analysis to record it, because the question is when the document arrived, at what time during the night, and whether all the people in the service were at their respective positions. However, the real answer to that question can only be given by the gentleman from the Security Administration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. You accept that you are speculating. Thank you. Yes, Madam Vidovic, you can proceed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document can be removed, Your Honour. Could we now have a look at document D725, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, could you please have a look at this document. It has to do with taking measures, certain measures. The document is entitled "Proposal." The date is the 6th of March, 1995, Zenica. So could we please go to the second page of the English version, and could the witness see the signature. Witness, can you see this? This is a proposal to take certain measures. Could the document please be scrolled up a bit. That's right, thank you. It says here: "Taking POPO and TK." Do you remember this document, Witness?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what this is, "POPO" and "TK"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: "PO" and then this other "PO," it is "Previous Operative Processing." That means that this person was a suspect from earlier on, and in order for more operative work to be done in a proper way, we are asking the Security Administration to act on this, and we are suggesting that that person's telephone be listened in to and other measures taken.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Very well, thank you. I do apologise. Witness, could you please have a look at the second paragraph in this letter now, the second paragraph underneath "Proposal"?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, a larger group of individuals had been identified. Is that what you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you about that. Do you agree that activities of the El Mujahedin Detachment, according to your proposal, are being linked to the activity of foreign intelligence agencies?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You mention in your proposal that Mujahedin are coming through various points in European countries and then to the Republic of Croatia, where they're ultimately selected and then sent on to the Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You also say that from time to time they use UN IDs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the essence of this document is that the El Mujahedin is acting on behalf of foreign intelligence agencies, and that is why you're asking for measures to be taken?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Certainly, that is reasonable doubt, and it is to be confirmed, corroborated.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right. Your Honours, could this document please be assigned an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Go ahead.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Just one question in relation to this document, just one more, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree that the Security Administration of the General Staff accepted your security and proposed to your commander -- or, rad, rather, asked the commander of the General Staff to use special methods and resources that you suggest in this request?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I don't see what the chief of the Security Administration wrote up here, but since this processing did exist and it could not have taken place without a report and other documents, this is just one of the prescribed documents in applying methods and resources, and I am answering your question in the affirmative.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What will follow after that is the Vranduk operative action; is that right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the document be assigned an exhibit number, and I think it's now time for the break.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 939.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. May I just confirm. I was approached by the Legal Officer in Chambers that there's a desire to finish with this witness and that maybe we could sit from 3.00 to half past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm told it's confirmed, so we will sit at 3.00. Court adjourned, and come back at 3.00. --- Luncheon recess taken at 1.45 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Before the break, Witness, we mentioned the Vranduk action. Your Honours, can we have Exhibit 693 now. 693 is under seal. Therefore, may we please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: We're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] For the record, this is actually Exhibit 933. That is the exhibit number, I believe. This is information produced by the Military Security Administration. The date is the 17th of May, 1995.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So, Witness, have a look, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I have.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It's got your name on it, doesn't it?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I can't quite see.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I believe you've seen this document already today. It was shown to you by the OTP, and I want to ask you a question.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: The header and everything else that this report comprises belongs to the Military Security Department of the 3rd Corps.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Fine. Could you please look at the first two paragraphs, in that case, the first two paragraphs of this document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can we please zoom in in such a way as for us to be able to see the first two paragraphs. Thank you. Your Honours, it's the first two paragraphs on this page. Right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Is it correct to say, just for the record, to correct what was said a little earlier, that it is dated the 10th of May, 1995, and not the 17th?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, there's a different date at the top. If we could please scroll down so that we get to see that portion. It's actually a document dated the 17th. Can we please go back to the first page in the English as well.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You see, Madam Vidovic, what happened is you first called P2083, and then you said actually it's Exhibit 933. I also thought P2083 was dated the 17th, but Exhibit 933 is definitely dated the 10th.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, in that case I would prefer to be looking at 2083, PT2083, right now, and you have my apologies. And you have my apologies. The document is very similar. My apologies. That's the one.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, can you see that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes, the document.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine. Can we please scroll down to the very end of this document, and then the next page in English, page 2.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Can you please look closely and tell me if you're familiar with the substance of this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Indeed, I am.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Fine, fine. Can we take the English back to page 1.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, can you please look at the first two short paragraphs, the first two. You agree, don't you, that here you convey information or register information, whichever way you like? This was probably a phone conversation that was intercepted, and you obtained information about contact between Abu Maali and the Efendi Alilovic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Likewise, Alilovic requested the detachment commander to take the Zenica mufti, Halil Mehtic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The document also suggests that visits are being arranged. Can you tell us, what is "efendi"? Efendi, do you agree with me, is an Islamic religious official; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: The Zenica mufti, this is the highest Islamic religious title in the area; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Zenica area.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and further afield as well.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ah, further afield too. This is not just the Zenica area, this is the Zenica --

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: There is a certain amount of overlap between the two areas.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you agree that you had certain information on contacts between the platoon commander, contacts of this kind, and the Zenica mufti?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let me go back to the issue of the El Mujahedin Detachment. Do you agree with me that you had a lot of information like this that indicated that there were links between the detachment, on the one hand, and individual members of the Islamic religious community, high-ranking ones; you agree with that, don't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you not agree, then, that this made the entire problem a very complex one to solve?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do agree.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, would I be right in stating that here was a person or an institution who, in the Zenica area, enjoyed the support of high-ranking Islamic leaders? This support was enormous because that meant all the people were behind this person, then; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree, you're right. It's about all the details that I spoke of. It's about how those contacts worked and how the whole thing functioned, inter-marrying, that kind of thing. That constituted a huge problem.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Let's leave these mixed marriages aside for the time being, sir. I'm talking about the support they received from the highest-ranking leaders of the Muslim community, religious officials. That's what I'm saying, their support to the detachment.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's true.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the conditions being what they were, any direct clashes with the detachment would have driven a rift among the -- created a rift among the Bosnian people, Bosnian people of Central Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, and I've stated that myself on a number of different occasions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, can we please have a number for this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 940.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can the witness now look at D726, please. This is an information of the Military Security Department of the 7th of July [as interpreted], 1995, and it calls the security -- it's called: "The security aspects of the movements and presence of foreigners and representatives of humanitarian organisations in Zenica municipality." And if we can take a look at the last page of this document where the stamp is, or rather, not the stamp, but the signature, the last page of the document where the signature should be, in English also, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: I simply note for the transcript, I don't know if this was an interpretation error, line 10, page 105 makes reference to the 7th of July, and I believe the document is dated the 7th of June.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Indeed. Thank you very much, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. I did say "June." Thank you, my learned friend.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: You did, ma'am. It's the transcript, itself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please, do you recognise this document? Is it your document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, it's information signed by me. It was created in the Military Security Service, and Osman Vlajcic was the person who dealt with this material.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can we go back to page 1, both in English and B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you first look at the introductory part, where it says: "On the 24th of May, 1995, a meeting was held attended by representatives of civilian authorities, representatives of the Party of Democratic Action and the Islamic religious community." Do you see that?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now please look at paragraph 4. It's a little longer.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we scroll down in English so that we can see the paragraph starting with the words: "The common assessment ..." Or: "The joint assessment ..." Can we scroll up a little bit? And it continues on the next page. It's: "Everyone agreed ..."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Could you read this, Witness, paragraph 4?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes. "Everyone agreed that ..." or "It was agreed that..."

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: No, I thought could you read it silently to yourself, Witness, please.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I've read it.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Do you agree that the security aspect of the movement and sojourn of foreigners and humanitarian organisations was considered?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And everyone agreed that there is non-application of the existing legal provisions in relation to Arabs; is this correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And then there are opinions expressed that documents are being issued too easily, allowing these people to stay in Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And the lack of appropriate inspection after approvals have been issued was mentioned, as to whether these persons were complying with the regulations?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, all the problems mentioned here, these are problems having to do with lack of compliance with the laws and regulations, with the legislation; the civilian authorities were not complying with regulations when it came to Arabs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So the organs mentioned here are municipal civilian authorities which were in charge of issuing permits and inspecting the compliance with regulations?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, the municipal authorities and the military district. These were the people who were in the government.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You said "military district"? It says "military" in the -- what did you say?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Districts, they were districts, a higher form of local self-government higher than municipalities. That's the kind of district I was referring to.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So these were civilian authorities?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Well, now they're at cantonal rank, they are higher-level authorities.

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Now, please take a look at the fifth paragraph from the top. I'll quote just one sentence: "It was observed that in cases where the competent organ reacts to such occurrences, there is no appropriate reaction by the next competent organ, the next higher-up organ?"

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: That's paragraph 2 in the English version, Your Honours. So when it came to the problem of the Arab factor in Central Bosnia, do you agree that there was a major problem, in that the civilian authorities were giving major support to the Arabs?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honours, could this document be admitted into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 941.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I would like to move on now to a different topic. Could the witness see D728, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, for the record, this is information from the Security Department of the 3rd Corps. It's dated the 29th of July, 1995, and it refers to criminal reports filed against members of the 328th Mountain Brigade in the time period from the 13th to the 21st of July, 1995. Could we please look at page 2 of the document, both in B/C/S and English. Mr. Alihodzic, did you sign reports such as this one?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, yes, I did.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Can we go back to page 1, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: These are criminal reports pertaining to only one brigade, and please look at the first paragraph in this document. In a very brief period of time, only eight days, it appears, nine criminal reports were filed?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Ten.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Ten, against ten members of the 328th Mountain Brigade?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Nine of whom or nine of which were for desertion. And now I would like to ask you the following in connection with this: Do you agree that this document shows that the 3rd Corps at this time had major problems with people acting on their own initiative, of their own will, simply leaving?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, I agree. I can give you numbers. It would pertain to up to 70 per cent of the Corps members.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: In what period?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Well, 700 to 800 men were being sought after in the period while I was there. That's while I was there.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It would appear from this that the 328th Brigade was not a highly-disciplined brigade?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Certainly.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I wish to tender this document into evidence.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: D728 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 942.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could the witness now look at D729, please. This is information sent from the Military Security Service Administration, dated the 10th of April, 1995, submitted to the chiefs of the military security services of the Corps, including the 3rd Corps. At that time, you were at the head of the 3rd Corps; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well. Could we please look at the title page of the document.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You will agree that it refers to some typical negative occurrences in the army units in March 1995 and that this is sent for the information of the Military Security Service in the Corps so that they can take preventive measures. And now let's look at page 2 both in English and the B/C/S, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please look at the document and look at the second paragraph, describing these typical negative occurrences, and it enumerates failure to report for duty by a large number of soldiers on one and the same day. And then if you look at the next paragraph, it describes willful abandonment of positions in certain units. And could you please look at the third page of the document, in English as well as B/C/S. Look at the last paragraph in the Bosnian version, please, which mentions refusal to obey orders, and it says that an entire battalion of the 1st Corps refused to obey an order issued by the 1st Corps commander?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] And could we look at the next page of the document, please. In English, we can keep the same page.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Look at where it describes the situation in the 115th Brigade. In English, it's the third paragraph, Your Honour, where it describes the situation in the 155th Brigade, and it says that out of 280 soldiers, not even 156 turned up for the lineup, and the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: We would object on relevance grounds. These units are all in the 1st Corps. I fail to see how they relate to this case and how this witness would be in a position to comment upon these statistics or numbers with respect to the 1st Corps.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, first of all, General Delic is not indicted as the 3rd Corps commander, and he is not being held responsible only for that. He is being held responsible as a commander of the General Staff. The document is relevant because I wish to demonstrate the sort of problems that General Delic and the General Staff were struggling with at the time. That's why it's relevant. As to how this particular witness can comment on it, this witness has just confirmed that he received this document, and I wish to know whether he's aware of these problems.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I'm halfway with you, I'm halfway with him. I'll tell you why. I hear what you say, that General Delic is charged in his capacity as a commander of the Army and not of the Corps. However, he's charged specifically with crimes committed within the 3rd Corps. So to that extent, I wish I could split myself.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honour, if I may add, the Prosecutor cannot say that Commander Delic was supposed to deal only with problems of the 3rd Corps in 1995. I'm trying to establish what the priorities of General Delic were, as a commander of the Main Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: I will overrule the objection. You agree?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I wanted to add that I fully agree. If we look at the efficiency of the control, then that could be relevant.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, could you now please look at the last paragraph in the Bosnian version on this page, and that's the next paragraph in the English version, which says that that over the past months, suicides were registered in some units, and then it says that one soldier of the 3rd Corps killed a commander. So you know of events not only in your own corps but in the Army of Bosnia-Herzegovina at the time. Were you aware of such incidents?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I knew about such incidents from at least two sources or, rather, three, three sources. One source was the chain of reporting in the Military Security Service to the Security Service Administration, and then the administration would send information back to us through their bulletins. And, furthermore, some of these units in the 1st Corps were sometimes inside the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. When Sarajevo was under siege, we assisted each other with logistics and so on. And the fourth source was in contacts with the security chief of their units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Witness. The problems described here, were these problems similar to the ones that existed in your corps?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, these were major problems. There were about 35.000 men, and of these, about 800 to 1.000 were being sought because they had abandoned their positions.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: And there were a lot of problems like this all over Bosnia?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct. Because human resources were being used to search for these men, the defence lines were not manned properly. This was reflected in morale and the combat readiness of the units.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Your Honour, I wish to tender this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Document 729 is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 943.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] 2415, please, document P2415.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Mr. Alihodzic, this is a document from the Security Services Centre based in Zenica. The date is the 18th of September, 1995, and it was sent to "The 3rd Corps Command, Military Security Department. Chief of CSB, Sefik Dzaferovic." You see that down there, don't you? At this time, you were the still with the Corps, weren't you?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: What about the chief of CSB, Mr. Dzaferovic, was he head of the CSB at the time still?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: All right. Do you remember that you received a report providing a list of incidents perpetrated by members of the 3rd Corps, between January and August 1995?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: By all means. Security-related issues were sent through the commander to the security organ.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: So you've seen this document?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: I actually have this document in my possession.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, could we please now look at page 2 in both the B/C/S and the English. Thank you. This document contains a list of incidents caused by 3rd Corps members. The first municipality listed is Zavidovici.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, please go through this -- go through this document, which in this particular portion describes incidents that occurred in Zavidovici Municipality, and try to focus particularly on sections that mention the El Mujahedin unit. The English continues on the next page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Can we go on to the next page in the English, please.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Witness, you will agree that this document talks about incidents that occurred between January and August 1995 in Zavidovici; is that true?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you actually count them, you will see that there were a total of nine such incidents; right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: If you look at this total, can you count them, please?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Nine, you're right, nine it is.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: Only the second-to-last, dated the 18th of July, 1995, on this list was perpetrated by a member of the El Mujahedin Detachment, Edin Huskic?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Indeed.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: It reads: "Edin Huskic willfully chased a student away from the beach and then left the scene."

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: You will agree with me that the preponderant majority of the incidents was actually caused by other BH Army unit members, as opposed to Edin Huskic; am I right?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I have no further questions for this witness. Can we just have a number for this document, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: The document is admitted into evidence. May it please be given an exhibit number.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, Exhibit number 944.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Mr. Mundis, any re-examination?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No re-examination. Thank you, Mr. President.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Judge.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Two brief questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Witness, where is Tesanj? Is it in the same area as Zeljezno Polje? Those are two different areas?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
