utterances.text: My apologies, Your Honour. It is in the area of the 3rd Corps. Tesanj and Zeljezno Polje are both in the area of responsibility of the 3rd Corps. The answer to that is, yes, that's Tesanj Municipality, and Zeljezno Polje was part of, I no longer remember myself, Zepce or Zenica. It was either Zepce or Zenica.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. One other brief question. On page 108, lines 1, 2, 3, I believe, of the transcript, there is something which I haven't quite understood. I was wondering if you could shed some light on this for us. Here, you, on page 107, line 22, you talked about military districts. Do you remember?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: No, I don't remember the terminology.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Let me remind you that you said --

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] If I may be of assistance, I spotted that, and this was an obvious interpretation error, because in the Bosnian the witness never used the words "military district." He just said "district," not "military."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So you do confirm that you were talking about a district, you weren't talking about a military district but a civilian one?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: This is probably a question that was about the position of religious dignitaries and how to explain what the position of a mufti would have been, and then the kind lady started talking about the efendi, the imam. He, as such, could be defined or appointed for a particular village, but at the same time this efendi, given his experience, work and time spent in the religious service, can also be defined as the principal imam in a certain area, and this can cover the area of a certain local commune or municipality. The mufti, on the other hand, has a number of municipalities under him, so that's what it meant. These areas, in a purely administrative sense, most frequently did not coincide with the division, in political and social terms, and by that I mean municipalities and cantons.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] When you're talking about districts that were a higher form of government or self-government, local self-government, which was above the municipalities, you are then talking about a civilian breakdown, not a military structure?

utterances.speaker: EKREM ALIHODZIC
utterances.text: That's right, that's right.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE LATTANZI
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Any questions arising, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: No, Mr. President, we'd like to just simply thank the witness for testifying.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Why are we getting a French interpretation on an English channel?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreter apologises.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: It certainly wasn't me, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, I know it wasn't you. Okay, you don't have to apologise, interpreter. It's just something that happens with technology, maybe. We should forgive. Okay, Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] None, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Sir, that brings us to the end of your testimony. Thank you very much for coming to testify in this matter. You are now excused, you may stand down, and please travel well back home.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Mundis.

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: Mr. President, I am aware of the time. There's just one housekeeping matter that I'd like to raise in private session before we adjourn for the week, if I may.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: May the matter please move -- the Chamber please move into private session.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Your Honours, we're now in open session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Thank you very much. I just want to use this time, because we technically have more than 30 minutes to go, according to our schedule, but we're not going to take all that time, just to talk about the recess. I have been sort of advised by the Chamber staff that there are some requests about when we should resume the trial next year because of problems that may be arising amongst the members of the parties. Is this something that you would like to talk about in private session or is it something you would like to talk about in open session? Can we start with you, Mr. Mundis?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: The Prosecution has no particular issues with respect to timing. It's, I believe, an issue for the Defence and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Madam Vidovic.

utterances.speaker: MS. VIDOVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Your Honours, I ask to start, if possible, on the 15th of January. You will be familiar with the problems already. The last time, it was in the paper, so ...

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: No, you don't have to go into the details. That is the request. What's your position on that request?

utterances.speaker: MR. MUNDIS
utterances.text: That is certainly a reasonable request, as far as the Prosecution is concerned, Your Honours. We leave it in the Trial Chamber's hands.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: Okay. Madam Vidovic, your request is granted. We will then resume on the 15th of January next year. Okay. That was all the housekeeping from the Bench. Shall we then adjourn? If we do, we are adjourning to Tuesday, the 4th of December, at 9.00 in the morning in Courtroom II. Court adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MOLOTO
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Tuesday, the 4th day of December, 2007, at 9.00 a.m. 20 21 22 23 24
